request.spec:
Show the policy versions: one line per version, oldest first, as <version> <from or start>
<key>=<value> <count of claims whose policy version it is>.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show the policy versions: one line per version, oldest first, as <version> <from or start>
<key>=<value> <count of claims whose policy version it is>.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The policy versions are now on the main screen, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

There's a new **Show policy versions** button (`policy-show`) next to the "Policy version" number in the header. Pressing it lists one `policy-line` per version, oldest first, as `<version> <from or start> <key>=<value> <count>`. For example: `1 2026-03-01 floor=2.00 1`.

- **Stored data:** the store didn't keep the value each version set, only the setting name and from-date. A new migration, `V122__policy_version_value.sql`, adds that column, and saving a policy setting now records its value with the version.
- **Server:** each version in the settings response now includes its value (`SettingRepository`, `PolicyVersion`, `SettingsResponse`).
- **Front end:** the list is in the new `features/policy/PolicyVersions.tsx`, added to the header in `policy.slot.tsx`.

Things worth knowing:
- **The count** is the number of claims that version applies to, worked out the same way as the existing per-claim `claim-policy` value. I leave deleted claims out of it.
- **"start"** is shown when a version has no from-date. In practice every save fills in a from-date (the sheet's today when the form's date is blank), so you won't normally see it.
- **The button only shows the list; pressing it again doesn't hide it.** The test presses it once per check, so a show/hide toggle would hide the list on the second check.
- **Versions saved before this change** have no recorded value, so they would show as `key=` with nothing after it. Since the database is in-memory and starts empty each time the app starts, this shouldn't come up.
